tour.name: Huahine Private Island Tour: Marae of Maeva, Sacred Blue-Eyed Eels, Stone Fish Traps & Vanilla

tour.overview:
Huahine, in the Leeward Islands, is often called the 'garden island': two green islands joined by a bridge, with quiet villages, few hotels and a lagoon of every shade of blue. It holds one of the richest concentrations of archaeological sites in Polynesia, around the village of Maeva, where the chiefs of the island once lived together, and its people keep traditions that have faded elsewhere.

This private half-day shows Huahine's culture and nature with a local guide and a vehicle.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 4 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Huahine or Fare
• Type: private tour with local guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Maeva marae.
• The stone fish traps.
• The eels of Faie.
• A vanilla plantation.
• A pearl farm.

WHY THIS WORKS
Huahine’s sites are little signposted; a local guide brings them and their stories to life.

WHO IT SUITS
Culture lovers, families and travellers seeking an authentic island.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the lagoon, ask us for a boat day with a motu picnic.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Huahine is about 40 minutes by plane from Papeete and is often combined with Bora Bora or Raiatea.

days.name: Maeva and its marae, the fish traps, the eels of Faie, vanilla and pearls
days.description:
What to expect: the archaeology and traditions of Huahine, with a local guide and private vehicle.

Your guide collects you at about 8:30 and drives to Maeva, by the Fauna Nui lake. Along the shore and on the slopes of Matairea hill are dozens of marae, stone temple platforms where each chiefly family worshipped, and a reconstructed fare pote'e, a traditional meeting house, now a small museum. In the channel, V-shaped stone fish traps, built centuries ago, still catch fish as the tide flows.

At the village of Faie, you meet the sacred eels, with startling blue eyes, which live in the river and are fed by the villagers. You visit a vanilla plantation, where your guide explains how each flower is pollinated by hand, and a pearl farm on the lagoon. You stop at the Belvedere viewpoint over Maroe Bay and the two islands, and end in Fare, the main village, with its quay and small shops.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up.
09:00 – Maeva marae and fish traps.
10:15 – Eels of Faie.
10:45 – Belvedere viewpoint.
11:15 – Vanilla plantation.
12:00 – Pearl farm.
12:45 – Fare.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A lagoon boat trip can be added in the afternoon.
• The beaches of Avea Bay are perfect for a swim.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, local guide, plantation and pearl farm visits, fruit, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, purchases, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: fruit tasting.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How do we get to Huahine?
faq.answer: By Air Tahiti, about 40 minutes from Papeete, or by inter-island ferry.

faq.question: Are the eels safe?
faq.answer: Yes. They are fed by the villagers and used to people; your guide shows you how to feed them.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No. Your guide suggests a restaurant in Fare or by the beach.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the eels. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. Most sites are near the road.

faq.question: Can we add a lagoon trip?
faq.answer: Yes, with snorkelling and a motu picnic.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: Only the pearl farm, with no obligation to buy.

faq.question: Is Huahine quiet?
faq.answer: Yes. It is one of the most authentic and least developed islands of the Society group.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, comfortable shoes, a hat and sun cream.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. May to October is drier.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not customary in French Polynesia and is never expected, but a small gesture for excellent service is always appreciated.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
